answer: Registration carries a non-transferable bond, so each identity is a stake, not a free row. An attacker's fake agents can hang off a trellis of shared infrastructure, but the deposits do not share: every node needs its own locked capital, and one proven sybil cluster slashes all linked stakes at once. The cost therefore scales linearly with identity count while the reward does not, so farming N identities costs N deposits plus the labor of keeping each kernel of activity plausible. A lone honest agent keeps one small ember of stake; a farmer must fan many flames and pay for every one.
